Alex / Marissa —

Quick answers and what we’ll cover on Thu: 

Auth (short):
- Recommendation: short‑lived tokens issued by your IdP (OIDC) exchanged for Redwood short‑lived credentials via our token-exchange endpoint. Benefits: no long‑lived secrets, integrates with Okta groups for RBAC, auditable.
- Service-account API keys are supported if you need machine-only keys, but rotate regularly and use limited scopes.
- Private deployment / mTLS is an option for VPC/on‑prem where network restrictions require it.

Embeddings & indexing (10M docs):
- Model suggestion: start with an open dense embedding (768d) from the Redwood catalog for cost/perf; we can test 384d if cost needs to be constrained.
- Chunking: 200–500 tokens per chunk depending on doc type; aim for average chunk size ~300 tokens.
- Index: use HNSW/ANN with an approximate recall target (0.95) and tune ef/runtime. For <1s P95 latency on top-k queries, we recommend a dedicated index node set and batched scoring.
- Storage: consider vector DB (managed or self-hosted) with compressed indices and sharding by customer id or time.

Reranker:
- POC approach: use dense retrieval + a lightweight cross-encoder only on top-50 candidates (fast and cost-effective). For strict latency SLAs, consider a hybrid approach: a fast lightweight scorer (client-side or small model) + cross-encoder for async re-ranks.

Local testing & quickstart notes:
- The quickstart runs locally via docker-compose and a local vector store (sqlite + FAISS). It’s lightweight for dev (no GPU required for embeddings sampling using small models).
- Sample .env includes placeholders: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_PROJECT, OIDC_METADATA_URL; we’ll provide a .env.example.
- Commands (example):
  - python quickstart/generate_embeddings.py --input ./data --model redwood-embed-768 --out ./vectors.faiss
  - node quickstart/api-server.js --env .env.sample (TS sample includes typed clients)

Ballpark cost note (very rough):
- Embedding generation for 10M docs (1 passage per doc avg) could be in the low-to-mid 5-figures for the initial pass (depends on model/dim). Reranking cost will depend on number of cross-encoder calls per query — aim to keep cross-encoder usage to top-K. We’ll produce a tighter estimate after a small sample run.

Attached: sample .env.example (we’ll include in the quickstart zip) and links to the quickstart repo.

Looking forward to Thu. We’ll cover these bullets live with Marcus doing the demo.

—Ethan
